lines.text: A request can name a voltage, or it can name a target.
In Tuner X, you picked Motion Magic, gave it a position, and watched the arm speed up, cruise, and slow down into place.
In code, it's the same swap. The voltage request comes out, and a Motion Magic request goes in.
Your gains come from the bench. Out of the box every one of them is zero, so paste your config from Tuner X again.
The commands change too. Instead of a voltage, this one names a place: straight up.
And the release binding comes out. You'll see why in a second.
Hold the trigger. The motor plans the whole move, then follows it: speed up, cruise, slow down, arrive.
Now let go. The command ends, and the request stays on the motor, just like last time.
But this time the request is a position, so staying is exactly what holds the arm up.
Try letting go halfway through the move.
It still finishes. The motor already knows where the arm is supposed to end up.
If the arm doesn't move at all, the gains are still zero. If it overshoots and hunts, retune in Tuner X and paste again. Don't fix it in code.
Name where the arm should be, and the motor keeps it there, even after the command ends.
